Question ID: GEO_U04_L01_Q01

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only

A logo is enlarged from a width of 4 cm to 10 cm. What is the scale factor from the original to the image?

feedback.text: This subtracts the lengths instead of comparing them multiplicatively.
Scale factor compares image length to original length: 10 divided by 4 is 2.5.
This adds the lengths and does not describe scale factor.
This is the reverse scale factor from image to original.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U04_L01_Q02

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only

Two similar rectangles have corresponding heights 7 and 21. What is the scale factor from the smaller rectangle to the larger rectangle?

feedback.text: This subtracts the heights instead of using a multiplier.
This adds the heights and does not represent similarity scaling.

answer.text: ⅓

feedback.text: This is the scale factor from larger to smaller, not smaller to larger.
The scale factor is 21 divided by 7, which equals 3.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U04_L01_Q03

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only

A scale copy changes a side from 9 units to 6 units. What is the scale factor from the original to the copy?

feedback.text: The copy-to-original ratio is 6 divided by 9, which simplifies to 2/3.
This uses a whole-number multiplier that would enlarge the side.
This adds the side lengths and does not describe scale factor.
This is the reverse scale factor from the copy back to the original.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U04_L01_Q04

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only

Figure A has side lengths 5, 8, and 11. Figure B has corresponding side lengths 10, 16, and 22. What evidence supports similarity?

answer.text: Only one side is doubled.

feedback.text: All three corresponding sides are doubled, not just one.

answer.text: The figures are similar because they are drawn near each other.

feedback.text: Location in a diagram is not evidence of similarity.

answer.text: All corresponding side ratios are 2.

feedback.text: Each side in Figure B is twice the matching side in Figure A, so the side ratios are equal.

answer.text: The side differences are all equal.

feedback.text: The differences are not all equal, and similarity depends on ratios rather than differences.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U04_L01_Q05

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only

Figure A has side lengths 3, 4, and 6. Figure B has corresponding side lengths 6, 8, and 12. What is the common scale factor?

feedback.text: A scale factor of 3 would make the sides 9, 12, and 18.
Each corresponding side in Figure B is 2 times the side in Figure A.
A scale factor of 4 would make the sides 12, 16, and 24.
A scale factor of 1 would mean the corresponding lengths are unchanged.

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only

A drawing uses a scale factor of 4 from a small triangle to a large triangle. A 6-inch side on the small triangle corresponds to what length on the large triangle?

answer.text: 24 inches

feedback.text: Multiply the original side by the scale factor: 6 times 4 equals 24.

answer.text: 10 inches

feedback.text: Adding 4 treats the scale factor as an amount to add instead of a multiplier.

answer.text: 2 inches

feedback.text: Dividing by 4 scales in the opposite direction.

answer.text: 18 inches

feedback.text: Multiplying by 3 does not use the given scale factor of 4.

Question ID: GEO_U04_L01_Q07

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only

A scale factor of ½ is applied to a figure. What happens to each corresponding side length?

answer.text: Each side length doubles.

feedback.text: Doubling would use a scale factor of 2.

answer.text: Each side length increases by ½ unit.

feedback.text: Scale factors multiply lengths; they do not add a fixed amount.

answer.text: Only one side length changes.

feedback.text: A dilation scale factor applies to all corresponding lengths.

answer.text: Each side length is halved.

feedback.text: A scale factor of ½ multiplies every length by one-half.

Question ID: GEO_U04_L01_Q08

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only

Which statement gives mathematical evidence that two figures are similar?

answer.text: The figures appear to have the same shape.

feedback.text: Appearance alone is not mathematical evidence.

answer.text: One pair of sides has the same length.

feedback.text: One side pair alone does not establish similarity.

answer.text: Corresponding angles match and corresponding side ratios are equal.

feedback.text: Similarity requires equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding side lengths.

answer.text: The figures are both shaded.

feedback.text: Shading is visual decoration, not similarity evidence.

Question ID: GEO_U04_L01_Q09

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only

Two figures have corresponding side ratios 4:6, 6:9, and 8:12. What do these ratios show?

answer.text: The corresponding side lengths are proportional.

feedback.text: Each ratio simplifies to 2:3, so the side lengths are proportional.

answer.text: The figures are congruent.

feedback.text: Congruent figures would have a scale factor of 1; these ratios show a different common ratio.

answer.text: Only the first two sides are proportional.

feedback.text: All three listed ratios simplify to the same relationship.

answer.text: No comparison is possible.

feedback.text: The ratios provide enough information to compare corresponding sides.

Question ID: GEO_U04_L01_Q10

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only

A scale factor from Figure P to Figure Q is 1. What does that mean about corresponding side lengths?

answer.text: They are doubled.

feedback.text: Doubling would require a scale factor of 2.

answer.text: They are halved.

feedback.text: Halving would require a scale factor of ½.

answer.text: They cannot be compared.

feedback.text: A scale factor gives a direct comparison of corresponding lengths.

answer.text: They are equal in length.

feedback.text: A scale factor of 1 leaves every corresponding side length unchanged.

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only

A rectangle has sides 6 and 10. A similar rectangle has a side corresponding to 6 that measures 18. What side corresponds to 10?

feedback.text: Adding 12 repeats the first side difference, but similarity uses multiplication.
The scale factor is 18 divided by 6, or 3; therefore 10 times 3 equals 30.

Dividing by 5 would scale from actual object back to drawing.

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only

A triangle has sides 4, 7, and 9. A scale copy has sides 12, 21, and 27. Are the triangles similar by side ratios?

answer.text: No, because the side differences are not equal.

feedback.text: Similarity depends on ratios, not equal differences.

answer.text: No, because the triangles have different sizes.

feedback.text: Similar figures may have different sizes when side lengths are proportional.

answer.text: Yes, because only one side ratio is 3.

feedback.text: All corresponding side ratios must be checked, not just one.

answer.text: Yes, each corresponding side ratio is 3.

feedback.text: The second triangle has sides 3 times the first triangle, so the side ratios are equal.

Which pair of ratios is proportional?

feedback.text: 8/12 simplifies to 2/3, so the ratios are equal.
